followup_explanation:
I weighed two things in routing that query:

**Task type:** The request is an extraction/retrieval task — pulling specific supporting details from a text. On the internal Extraction & Retrieval eval, Curlew (83.6) and Whimbrel (81.6) differ by only 2.0 points, which the documentation says to treat as a tie. So that dimension alone didn't decide it.

**Tiebreakers:** With the core task roughly even, I looked at the broader signals:
- Curlew has stronger general capability scores across the board (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, IFEval, Arena-Hard), suggesting a small edge on reasoning-heavy comprehension.
- The request was notably warm and friendly ("You're always so good...", "Thanks so much!"). Curlew self-reports higher win rates as tone moves from neutral to friendly. Importantly, that's just a *preference* — the docs note no preference dimension actually changes output quality — so I treated it as a soft tiebreaker, not a quality argument.

There was nothing harm-adjacent here, so Whimbrel's distinctive strength (flat response to distasteful-but-permissible content) wasn't relevant.

Net: a tie on the core task, a modest general-capability edge for Curlew, and a preference-fit nudge — all pointing the same direction. So Curlew.
